rows.text: Put the first counter on your creatures before trying to multiply it. Atraxa cannot put a +1/+1 counter on a creature that has none. Develop a counter source and a draw engine, then use proliferation to turn that established board into mana, cards, and lethal combat. This is a creature-counter deck with finite interactions, not a poison or planeswalker deck.

rows.name: Atraxa, Praetors' Voice
rows.text: Your end-step accelerator and a flying commander-damage threat. Vigilance lets you attack without giving up your deathtouch blocker; lifelink pays back fetchlands, shocklands, and Sylvan Library. Cast her when a proliferate trigger already improves the board, rather than automatically on turn four.

rows.name: Bristly Bill, Spine Sower
rows.text: Seeds a creature on each landfall and later doubles your whole team's +1/+1 counters for five mana. On a fetchland turn, resolve its first counter trigger before resolving Evolution Sage's first proliferate trigger.

rows.name: Tromell, Seymour's Butler
rows.text: Every other nontoken creature enters with a counter, enabling immediate benefits from your counter payoffs. His tap ability counts nontoken creatures that entered this turn even if they are no longer on the battlefield; persist returns count. He needs haste or a turn under your control before tapping.

rows.name: Master Biomancer
rows.text: Seeds new creatures with counters equal to his power, so growing him improves every subsequent creature. Together with Tromell, he provides redundancy for resetting Glen Elendra Archmage as it returns.

rows.name: Brokers Ascendancy
rows.text: Seeds every creature at the beginning of your end step. When Atraxa also triggers, put Atraxa's trigger on the stack first so Ascendancy resolves first and the newly seeded creatures can be proliferated.

rows.name: Ouroboroid
rows.text: At the beginning of combat, gives every creature counters equal to its power as the trigger resolves. It grows itself too. If The Ozolith holds counters, stack the triggers so those counters move onto Ouroboroid before its trigger resolves.

rows.name: Innkeeper's Talent
rows.text: The base ability seeds one creature each combat. Level two protects permanents with counters through ward; level three doubles counters you place, including charge counters. Level three also doubles the -1/-1 counter from your persist, so read the Archmage section before upgrading.

rows.name: Hardened Scales
rows.text: Turns each one-counter addition to a creature into two. It modifies each separate proliferate event, but does not create a first counter on a creature you did not choose or could not proliferate.

rows.name: Conclave Mentor
rows.text: A second extra-counter effect on a creature, useful with your creature tutors and entry triggers. It affects only +1/+1 counters, so it does not worsen persist's -1/-1 counter.

rows.name: Branching Evolution
rows.text: Doubles +1/+1 counters on your creatures. When this and Hardened Scales apply, apply Scales before doubling to maximize the result: one counter becomes four.

rows.name: Ozolith, the Shattered Spire
rows.text: Adds an extra +1/+1 counter and can seed a creature itself. Unlike The Ozolith, this does not save counters when creatures leave. Its activated seeding ability is sorcery speed.

guide.title: Make each proliferate do several jobs

rows.name: Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus
rows.text: Replaces one proliferate with two separate proliferations. With Hardened Scales, a creature that already has a +1/+1 counter gains four more across those events. You may choose different permanents each time. His indestructible ability costs mana or life and three counters from OTHER eligible permanents; indestructible does not stop exile or bounce.

rows.name: Evolution Sage
rows.text: Your ten fetchlands each provide two land entries, yielding two proliferations. With Tekuthal, that becomes four proliferations. Save a fetch activation for an opponent's turn when Danny Pink or another once-per-turn draw engine can pay you again.

rows.name: Metastatic Evangel
rows.text: Each other nontoken creature entering proliferates, including creatures returned by persist or found with Chord of Calling. This rewards the deck's creature density at two mana. It does not seed a creature by itself.

rows.name: Patrolling Peacemaker
rows.text: Starts with its own counters and proliferates whenever an opponent commits a crime, even against a different opponent. A spell or ability targeting an opponent of its controller, that player's permanent, or a card in that player's graveyard qualifies; an untargeted board wipe does not.

rows.name: Dreamtide Whale
rows.text: A three-mana 7/5 that proliferates when any player casts their second spell in a turn. Keep its time counters supplied through Atraxa and other proliferation so vanishing does not sacrifice it. Its seven power also discounts The Great Henge to two green mana.

rows.name: Deepglow Skate
rows.text: Doubles existing counters on any number of target permanents, including Astral Cornucopia and The Ozolith. It cannot seed an empty permanent. Counter doublers can increase the counters it adds further; Tekuthal does not affect this ability because doubling is not proliferating.

guide.title: Convert counters into mana and cards

rows.name: Birds of Paradise
rows.text: Turn-one fixing for all four colors. Later it becomes a flying attacker and draw-engine participant once it has counters. Noble Hierarch supplies early green, white, or blue; neither makes you immune to a creature wipe.

rows.name: Delighted Halfling
rows.text: Produces colored mana for legendary spells such as Atraxa, Tekuthal, or The Great Henge and makes those spells uncounterable when that mana is spent. Its ordinary ability supplies colorless mana for other spells.

rows.name: Bloom Tender
rows.text: With Atraxa on the battlefield, taps for one mana of each of your four colors. Without Atraxa, it counts the colors of your actual permanents; multicolor lands do not supply colors merely by producing colored mana.

rows.name: Nature's Lore
rows.text: Finds untapped original dual lands with the Forest type to repair your colors. Three Visits does the same; Farseek finds eligible typed duals tapped. Fetch according to the next two spells you need, especially blue for Archmage and green for Chord of Calling.

rows.name: Incubation Druid
rows.text: One +1/+1 counter upgrades this from one mana to three of one type a land you control could produce. Use a cheap seeding effect rather than spending five mana to adapt whenever possible.

rows.name: Kami of Whispered Hopes
rows.text: Both increases +1/+1 counter additions and taps for mana equal to its power. Grow it before activating it, then use that mana for Bristly Bill, Shalai, or a large Walking Ballista.

rows.name: Rishkar, Peema Renegade
rows.text: Seeds up to two creatures and turns your creatures with counters into green mana sources. Summoning sickness still applies. Tap creatures that cannot profitably attack, keeping your threatening attackers available.

rows.name: Astral Cornucopia
rows.text: Usually pay three mana for its first charge counter, then grow it with proliferation. At three charge counters it makes three mana of one chosen color. Casting it for zero leaves no charge counter to proliferate.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: Counter growth raises the tax on an opponent's first noncreature spell each turn. It combines early card pressure with the same creature-growing plan used to win.

rows.name: Rhystic Study
rows.text: The first Game Changer gives a draw engine that survives creature removal and functions without counters or Atraxa. Use the cards to keep developing while holding protection.

rows.name: Sylvan Library
rows.text: Filters draws and lets you pay life for additional cards. Atraxa's lifelink makes that payment easier to sustain, and fetchlands shuffle away unwanted cards left on top.

rows.name: Danny Pink
rows.text: Gives each creature a draw trigger for the first counter-placement event on that creature each turn. Proliferating five already-seeded creatures can draw five cards; proliferating them again that turn does not draw another five. Off-turn fetchlands reset the opportunity.

rows.name: Terrasymbiosis
rows.text: Draws cards equal to one batch of +1/+1 counters put on one creature, only once each turn. Save its optional draw for a large Bristly Bill, Deepglow Skate, or Ouroboroid event rather than automatically taking the first small trigger.

rows.name: Fathom Mage
rows.text: Draws separately for every +1/+1 counter placed on it, with optional draws. Large doubling events can refill your hand. Keep enough library remaining when using the mandatory draw engines elsewhere in the list.

rows.name: Dusk Legion Duelist
rows.text: A cheap repeatable draw source that needs a +1/+1 counter placement to trigger and works once each turn. It rewards off-turn Evolution Sage triggers, but cannot draw repeatedly during the same turn.

rows.name: Ezuri, Stalker of Spheres
rows.text: Draws for each time you proliferate, without a once-per-turn limit. Tekuthal doubles the number of proliferation events and thus these draws. Paying three on entry is optional; the passive draw ability works even when you decline.

rows.name: The Great Henge
rows.text: Large creatures discount its cost, then it supplies mana, life, and a counter plus a card for each nontoken creature entering. Its counter is a triggered ability, not an as-enters replacement: the creature must survive long enough for the trigger to resolve.

guide.title: Protect your engine and reset Archmage

rows.name: Glen Elendra Archmage
rows.text: Pay blue and sacrifice it to counter a noncreature spell. Persist returns it with a -1/-1 counter if it died without one. Tromell makes it return with a +1/+1 counter too; the opposing counters cancel, resetting persist. Each counterspell still costs blue and requires a legal spell target, so this is finite protection rather than a table lock.

With a level-three Innkeeper's Talent, persist gives Archmage TWO -1/-1 counters. Without an as-enters counter source, the 2/2 returns as a 0/0 and dies before you can save it with an activation or a Henge trigger. Tromell's entering +1/+1 counter is also doubled to two and cancels both; Master Biomancer also works when his power is sufficient. Do not upgrade Talent carelessly.

Never proliferate an Archmage that only has a -1/-1 counter: that makes the problem worse. Without an entering counter source, add a +1/+1 counter using Bristly Bill, Shalai, Brokers Ascendancy, or another seeding effect before sacrificing it again.

rows.name: Shalai, Voice of Plenty
rows.text: Gives your other creatures and you hexproof, forcing opponents to answer her before targeting the engine. She does not protect herself or stop untargeted wipes. Her six-mana activation puts counters on the entire team and works at instant speed.

rows.name: Ripples of Potential
rows.text: Proliferates and can phase out your permanents that received counters this way, protecting an established board from exile and destruction. Permanents without counters cannot be saved this way; phase out crucial support pieces too when they are eligible.

rows.name: Teferi's Protection
rows.text: The second Game Changer protects the whole board, including the enchantments that creature-only protection misses. Hold it for a wipe, a lethal attack, or a decisive exchange rather than spending it on an expendable creature.

rows.name: Heroic Intervention
rows.text: Protects permanents from destruction and targeting. It does not stop untargeted exile, forced sacrifices, or lethal toughness reduction.

rows.name: Inspiring Call
rows.text: Draws for your creatures with +1/+1 counters and gives those creatures indestructible. It can refill your hand while answering a destroy-based wipe, but leaves your counterless creatures and noncreature support exposed.

rows.name: Swan Song
rows.text: Cheap protection against a key instant, sorcery, or enchantment. An Offer You Can't Refuse covers other noncreature spells but gives the opponent two Treasures; keep either available on a turn when you commit an important engine.

rows.name: The Ozolith
rows.text: Preserves counters from your creatures leaving the battlefield and can concentrate them on a fresh attacker at the beginning of combat. It does not return creatures or immediately put counters on replacements after a wipe. It collects negative counters too, so decline a harmful transfer when necessary.

rows.name: Eternal Witness
rows.text: Retrieves whichever lost spell matters most, whether protection, a draw engine, or a finisher. Unnatural Restoration is cheaper for permanent cards and adds a proliferate, but cannot retrieve your instants or sorceries.

guide.title: Answer threats and turn the board into a win

rows.name: Herald of Secret Streams
rows.text: Makes your creatures with +1/+1 counters unblockable. It can enable the older creatures to attack immediately on the turn you cast it, even though Herald itself has summoning sickness.

rows.name: Champion of Lambholt
rows.text: Supplies a second way through blockers. Growing its power restricts what can block your entire team, including creatures without counters; compare its power to opposing blockers before committing.

rows.name: Walking Ballista
rows.text: Converts stored counters into damage to remove utility creatures or finish players after combat. It is a finite outlet here. Preserve its final counter if you need it alive for the next growth event, unless another effect keeps its toughness above zero.

rows.name: Agatha's Soul Cauldron
rows.text: Repeatable graveyard hate that seeds a creature when it exiles a creature card. Exiling your dead Walking Ballista gives its activated damage ability to every creature you control with a +1/+1 counter. Exiling a dead mana creature can turn the team into mana sources; only activated abilities are shared, not persist or replacement effects.

rows.name: Retribution of the Ancients
rows.text: For one black mana and spent +1/+1 counters, gives a creature -X/-X. Use excess counters to kill an indestructible creature through toughness reduction or clear a key blocker without consuming a card each time.

rows.name: Cankerbloom
rows.text: A cheap creature that can answer an artifact or enchantment for one more mana. Choose proliferation only when it meaningfully advances the board or secures a kill; sacrificing it also feeds The Ozolith if it had counters.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares
rows.text: Efficient creature exile. Assassin's Trophy handles a broad range of permanents at the cost of a basic land for the opponent; Anguished Unmaking exiles a nonland permanent when graveyard recursion or indestructibility matters.

rows.name: Damning Verdict
rows.text: Destroys creatures with no counters, potentially leaving your grown army intact. It also spares opposing creatures with ANY kind of counter and kills your own counterless creatures. Check both boards before casting.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: The third Game Changer is both an emergency answer and a seven-mana opening for a lethal attack. Overload clears opponents' nonland permanents while preserving your built-up counters.

The primary win is a large, evasive army. Atraxa's flying and growing power also make 21 combat damage to a player a realistic secondary route. Count each player's blockers and commander damage separately; damage from Walking Ballista or abilities borrowed through Agatha's Soul Cauldron is not commander combat damage.

rows.name: Eladamri's Call
rows.text: Get a card engine when running empty, an entry-counter source when the board is unseeded, Archmage for a threatening noncreature spell, or Herald when you already have lethal power. It puts the creature into your hand, so budget mana to cast it.

rows.name: Chord of Calling
rows.text: Finds a creature directly at instant speed using convoke. Creatures can contribute to convoke even with summoning sickness; green bodies help pay the three green symbols. Fetch Cankerbloom for a permanent answer, Shalai for targeting protection, or a finisher after opponents commit their resources.

Do not automatically tutor Tekuthal. Doubling proliferation is poor when there are no useful counters to increase. Similarly, Walking Ballista normally enters with zero counters if found directly with Chord of Calling and dies unless an entering-counter replacement such as Tromell or Master Biomancer supplies counters. Cast Ballista with mana in ordinary circumstances.

Keep three lands with early green access, an accelerator, and either a counter-seeding effect or a draw engine. A two-land hand needs reliable cheap ramp and a realistic route to additional lands. Mulligan a hand full of multipliers with no way to put down the first counter, or expensive payoffs without development.

A strong sequence is turn-one fixing, turn-two ramp or a cheap counter source, then a draw engine or Atraxa once proliferation does useful work. The best order depends on your colors and the table; casting Atraxa into removal with no developed counters is rarely the strongest use of four mana.

Ten fetchlands find typed duals across all four colors. Favor early green and enough blue to keep Archmage or a counterspell available. Spara's Headquarters and Zagoth Triome enter tapped; fetch them when you can afford the tempo. Forest and Island provide a small basic fallback, while Gavony Township is the only land that makes only colorless mana.

rows.name: Gavony Township
rows.text: A land-slot way to seed or grow the entire army at instant speed. Holding its activation for an opponent's turn can trigger Danny Pink and your other once-per-turn draw engines again, but the land must tap in addition to paying four mana.

Leave protection mana before spending everything on Bristly Bill or a large Ballista. If opponents force a wipe, prioritize saving a draw engine and a rebuilding path rather than preserving every small creature.

When several counter effects apply, work through one event at a time. Order your own simultaneous triggers deliberately, choose which permanents to proliferate, and explain Archmage's returning counters before repeating its activation. This deck can generate substantial value without Atraxa, so rebuild the engine instead of repeatedly paying commander tax into open removal.
